feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The evidence behind this design is iteration 7 (wheel_track 0.10, 50 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05, kp 3.75, ki 0.21, kd 0.375, base 1.15), which scored 399.7 with oval progress 0.995 and 20 of 20 finishes. Its s-bend and slalom max_error were 0.0676 and 0.0608 m, and neither track finished. Line losses stayed near 1 per run on the bend tracks (iteration 7: 1.65 and 1.0), so the tape is not being lost. Across iterations 0 to 7, bend max_error has stayed on a 0.059 to 0.068 m plateau under every span, footprint, lead, speed and wheel_track change. Iteration 0 (40 mm) and iteration 4 (50 mm) show progress is near its best at 40 to 50 mm, and iteration 3 (60 mm, 12 mm, weaker controller) fell to 0.275 on the oval, which is the risk for this candidate. Decide from the next race as follows. If oval progress holds at 0.65 or more and s-bend and slalom max_error both fall below about 0.06 m, keep the 60 mm span and tune the controller only. If oval progress falls below about 0.65 while steering oscillation is above about 0.35, the span has reduced the effective steering gain or added oscillation, so return to the 50 mm span (the current best) and tell the Integrator to lower kp first. If oval progress holds but bend max_error stays at or above 0.06 m with line losses near 1, the wider span does not limit the excursions, so the next test is a lead change to y 0.04 on the bend tracks only, not a further span change.
requested_changes: If oval progress is at or above 0.65 and s-bend and slalom max_error are both below 0.06 m, keep the 60 mm span (x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03) and wheel_track 0.10. Iteration 7 showed wheel_track 0.10 holds the oval at 0.995, and this result would be the first span-driven reduction in bend excursions.

If oval progress falls below about 0.65 with steering oscillation above about 0.35, revert to the 50 mm span at x = -0.025, -0.0125, 0, 0.0125, 0.025 with 12 mm footprints, y 0.05 and wheel_track 0.10. Iteration 4 (50 mm) reached oval progress 0.710 and iteration 3 (60 mm) fell to 0.275, so 60 mm is only worth keeping if it holds the oval.

If bend max_error stays at or above 0.06 m with oval progress held, keep the 60 mm span and change the lead only on the next candidate: sensor y from 0.05 to 0.04 with the same x positions and 12 mm footprints. Iteration 1 showed that y 0.03 collapses progress, so do not go below 0.04.
